verdict.rationale: WezTerm documents its own integrated SSH client: it makes ad-hoc connections, parses ~/.ssh/config, reuses one session across tabs, and offers SSH domains that connect to a remote wezterm multiplexer. Nothing in the evidence shows it transferring terminfo, injecting shell integration, or propagating local config to the remote host, which is the distinctive part of this story. missing for 10: automatic terminfo installation on the remote host, automatic shell-integration injection over SSH, config propagation to the remote, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can SSH to remote hosts with the terminal's own integration carrying my terminfo, shell integration, and config along

citations.quote: wezterm uses an embedded ssh library to provide an integrated SSH client. The client can be used to make ad-hoc SSH connections to remote hosts
A connection to a remote wezterm multiplexer made via an ssh connection is referred to as an _SSH domain_.
Creating new tabs or panes will each create a new channel in your existing session so you won't need to re-authenticate for additional tabs
